errors: In the 5/13 line of the middle column the printed transcription reads (2+3x)/(5+13x), which is not unimodular (det 11). Comparison with the bottom-right line suggests (2+5x)/(5+13x), with det 1; this is a transcription issue rather than Riemann's slip.
The transcription's (2+8x)/(9+13x) for 3/13 is not unimodular (det -46). The intended neighbour is 2/9, so it should read (2+3x)/(9+13x).
The constant factor 2 of delta Omega is dropped in the integrated-by-parts expression. This is harmless for the Euler-Lagrange condition.
In the related next-page computation, log(rho) is negative near rho = 0, so (log rho)^alpha should be read as (log 1/rho)^alpha. This is a sign convention, not an error of substance.
The phase values and the h/13 table cannot be checked without knowing the underlying function. Several readings (35/13, 57/13, -93/13) are uncertain.

results.what: Continued fraction 8/13 = [0;1,1,1,1,2] with convergents and Farey-neighbour (unimodular) adjacency
Parametrisation of all fractions adjacent to n'/n by (m'+x n')/(m+x n), with a phase linear in x, tracked along continued-fraction chains under mod-2/mod-4 parity conditions
results.modern_name: action of modular / theta-group matrices on cusps; bookkeeping of the multiplier system (root-of-unity factor) of theta/eta transformations
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1877 (eta multiplier, Dedekind sums), Hermite 1858 (theta multipliers), building on Riemann's fragment 'Grenzfaelle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen' (Nachlass XXVIII, publ. 1876 with Dedekind's commentary)

results.what: First variation of the Dirichlet integral and integration by parts giving Laplace's equation plus a boundary term; log r comparison estimates near a point
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle / Euler-Lagrange equation for the Dirichlet energy

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for Riemann's known (posthumously published) fragment on the limiting behaviour of modular functions at rational points, which Dedekind commented on. The Dirichlet-principle computation is standard Riemann. The concrete numerical phase tables are a modest unpublished detail, but nothing beyond what is attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: All corrected neighbour pairs used on the page are unimodular (det = ±1)

transcription_corrections: Middle column, 5/13 line: '(2+3x)/(5+13x)' should be '(2+5x)/(5+13x)', as in the bottom-right occurrence; only this is unimodular.
Bottom middle, 3/13 line: '(2+8x)/(9+13x)' should be '(2+3x)/(9+13x)', the neighbour of 3/13 being 2/9.
'n'-m'/n+m' in the left column is probably (n'-m')/(n-m), consistent with the header line.
'5/-8' in the phase list is the convergent 5/8 written with a sign, matching the signed-quotient expansions on the previous page.
'm' ungerade [?] n gerade' / 'm' gerade n' ungerade': parity conditions; the first word may read 'n' ungerade'.
The upside-down block: the first line is the boundary integral ∫(u_x δu dy - u_y δu dx) minus the area integrals of u_xx δu and u_yy δu, from integrating delta Omega by parts.
